newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel falls on Irish cargo deal.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel falls on Irish cargo deal.

text.p: A cargo deal from an Irish refinery to a German trader on Tuesday brought down straight-run fuel oil prices in Europe, traders said.
The 50,000 tonne cargo was heard traded at around $89.50 fob, well below the market, because it was very prompt. The material was believed headed transatlantic.
The deal thinned out supply and although the market looked weak, with refiners still preferring to process more profitable crude, traders said values were probably around $91/$93 fob.
Russian material was attracting buying. An M-40 went on Monday for 3 means flat to a British major, which was also heard to have picked up an E-4 out of Klaipeda at 3 means plus $2.50.
In the Mediterranean two Libyan straight-run cargoes were heard loading, with at least one on offer, while two Russian M-100 cargoes were seen coming available soon in Tuapse.
